newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FNB SAYS NOT IN TALKS ON SELLING STAKE.
newsitem.headline: FNB SAYS NOT IN TALKS ON SELLING STAKE.

text.p: First National Bank Holdings (FNB), one of South Africa's biggest four banks, said on Wednesday it was not involved in talks with any party on the sale of a stake in the bank.
FNB has been dogged by persistent rumours that Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd is keen to shed its 20.4 percent interest in the banking group.
"The truth of the matter is that we are not sitting down having any discussion with anyone," Viv Bartlett, FNB's managing director told Reuters.
He said the rumours, which were "unsettling", stemmed from perceptions that Anglo may wish to unbundle its non-core interests.
Peter Thompson, an executive director of FNB, said an opportunity to buy into the bank may have existed when the share price was at 19 rand, a level last seen in December last year.
"It is fair to say that when our share price was 19 rand there were a lot of good reasons for buying," Thompson said.
FNB's shares closed at 31.60 rand on Wednesday.
Financial markets have listed a number of possible suitors for Anglo's stake in FNB, including South African competitor bank, Nedcor Ltd , the U.K's Barclays Plc and Hong Kong Shanghai Bank .
A recent addition to the list has been acquisitive local financial group Investec Bank Ltd .

Poor earnings growth has been cited as another reason for a takeover. FNB on Wednesday reported a slim 6.7 percent increase in half year headline earnings to 110.4 cents a share, building on a narrow eight percent rise for the full year to end-September last year.
